# How to explore the organization's governance

Navigate the organization's governance structure: list its roles, read one by id, walk the role tree, drill into a circle's subroles, read a role's domains, policies, and projects, see who fills a role, roll up its sub-roles' fillers, and search across every resource type.

## Prerequisites

- A stored, usable token (the connection context is complete). If you are not authenticated, run `glassfrog auth login` first.
- The `glassfrog` binary on your `PATH`.

## Steps

### 1. List every role in the organization

```
glassfrog roles
```

Each role is printed as a projection. The list walks every page to completion by default. To see only the first page, add `--first-page`.

To narrow the list, add a filter:

```
glassfrog roles --parent role_aaaa
```

`--parent`, `--person`, `--tag`, and `--has-subroles` filter the list. They apply to the list only — passing one together with a role id is a usage error.

### 2. Read a single role by id

Take a role id from the list and read it:

```
glassfrog roles role_0123
```

The role's name, purpose, accountabilities, domains, and fillers are printed.

To embed related resources in the same call, add `--include` with a comma-separated list:

```
glassfrog roles role_0123 --include policies,subroles
```

The policies and subroles are printed inline within the role. Valid `--include` values for a role read are `assignments`, `subroles`, `parent_role`, `policies`, `notes`, and `skills`. See the [Role Reads reference](../../reference/role-reads.md) for every flag and projected field.

### 3. Read the organization tree

```
glassfrog tree
```

The tree is printed as a nested projection rooted at the anchor role. To focus on one branch, root the tree at a role:

```
glassfrog tree role_0123
```

To keep a large tree manageable, cap the depth:

```
glassfrog tree --depth 1
```

This prints the root and only its direct children. A child that has subroles below the cut is marked `(+ subroles below depth)` so it is distinguishable from a true leaf. To embed per-node resources, add `--include accountabilities,domains` (tree `--include` values are `accountabilities`, `domains`, `members`). See the [Organization Tree reference](../../reference/organization-tree.md) for full detail.

### 4. Drill into a circle's immediate subroles

```
glassfrog subroles role_0123
```

Each direct child role is printed as a projection — one level only. The list walks every page to completion by default; add `--first-page` to stop at one page. You can embed related resources per child with `--include assignments,policies`.

### 5. Read a role's domains and policies

A role's **domains** are the areas of control it holds; its **policies** are the rules governing its interior. Each has a paired list-and-single surface, keyed off different id types.

```
glassfrog domains role_0123
glassfrog policies role_0123
```

Both lists walk to completion by default and accept a full-text `--query`/`-q`:

```
glassfrog domains role_0123 --query marketing
glassfrog policies role_0123 --query "expense approval"
```

Take an id from either list and read it standalone — a domain by its `dom_…` id (optionally embedding its policies), a policy by its `pol_…` id (which prints the full body):

```
glassfrog domain dom_0123 --include policies
glassfrog policy pol_0123
```

See the [Role Domains reference](../../reference/role-domains.md) and [Role Policies reference](../../reference/role-policies.md) for every flag and projected field.

### 6. Read a role's projects

```
glassfrog projects role_0123
```

The list walks to completion by default and accepts three combinable filters — `--query`/`-q` (free text), `--status` (one of `archived`, `cancelled`, `completed`, `current`, `scheduled`, `someday`, `waiting`), and `--tag`:

```
glassfrog projects role_0123 --status current --tag q3
```

Read one project by its `proj_…` id for full detail:

```
glassfrog project proj_0123
```

This is the *role-owned* project surface; to read your own projects instead, use `glassfrog me projects`. See the [Role Projects reference](../../reference/role-projects.md).

### 7. See who fills a role, and roll up its sub-roles' fillers

To answer "who fills this role?" — with each filling's focus and election context:

```
glassfrog fillers role_0123
```

To roll up the actors filling a role's **direct sub-roles** (one level, not transitive):

```
glassfrog subrole-actors role_0123 --kind human
```

`fillers` returns the assignment shape (actor plus `focus` and `elected_until`); `subrole-actors` returns bare actor records (`id`/`name`/`kind`) and accepts a `--kind` filter (`agent` or `human`). Both walk to completion by default. See the [Role Fillers reference](../../reference/role-fillers.md) and [Subrole Filler Roll-up reference](../../reference/subrole-filler-roll-up.md).

### 8. Search across every resource type

When you don't know which role, policy, or project holds what you want, search the whole organization at once:

```
glassfrog search "strategy review"
```

Results come back ranked by relevance, each with a `type` badge and an id you carry into the matching per-resource read. Quote a multi-word query — an unquoted one is a usage error. Scope the search with `--types`:

```
glassfrog search "onboarding" --types policy,domain
```

Valid `--types` values are `role`, `note`, `project`, `action`, `skill`, `actor`, `policy`, and `domain`. See the [Cross-Model Search reference](../../reference/cross-model-search.md).

## Verify

- `glassfrog roles` prints each role and exits with code `0`. A multi-page org walks every page and prints all roles.
- `glassfrog roles role_0123` prints the role's name, purpose, accountabilities, domains, and fillers, and exits `0`. With `--include policies,subroles`, the request carries `include=policies,subroles` and those resources appear inline.
- `glassfrog tree` prints the nested projection rooted at the anchor role and exits `0`. `glassfrog tree --depth 1` carries `depth=1` and prints the anchor plus its direct children.
- `glassfrog subroles role_0123` prints each direct child role and exits `0`. On a leaf role it prints `No subroles.` and exits `0`.
- `glassfrog domains role_0123` / `glassfrog policies role_0123` print each domain/policy and exit `0`; on a role with none they print `No domains.` / `No policies.` and exit `0`. `glassfrog domain dom_0123` / `glassfrog policy pol_0123` print the single resource and exit `0`.
- `glassfrog projects role_0123` prints each project and exits `0`; with no matches it prints `no projects` and exits `0`. `glassfrog project proj_0123` prints the full detail and exits `0`.
- `glassfrog fillers role_0123` prints each filler (with focus and election context) and exits `0`; an unfilled role prints `no fillers` and exits `0`. `glassfrog subrole-actors role_0123` prints the rolled-up actors and exits `0`; when the sub-roles carry no fillers it prints `no actors` and exits `0`.
- `glassfrog search "strategy review"` prints results in relevance order and exits `0`; a query that matches nothing prints `No results.` and exits `0`.

Inspect the exit code after any command with `echo $?` — a clean read is `0`.

## Troubleshooting

**Not authenticated.** If no usable token is available, stderr reports `not authenticated` and points to `glassfrog auth login`, no data is printed, and the command exits with code `2`. Run `glassfrog auth login`, then retry.

**Unknown id.** Reading an id that does not exist (`glassfrog roles role_ffff`, `glassfrog domain dom_ffff`, `glassfrog policy pol_ffff`, `glassfrog project proj_ffff`, `glassfrog tree role_ffff`) prints the failure and the HTTP status to stderr and exits with a non-zero API-error code (`3`). Re-check the id against the list it came from. For `subrole-actors`, a **leaf anchor** (a role with no sub-roles) also surfaces as a `404` — it is not the same as an empty `0`-exit result, which means the sub-roles exist but carry no fillers.

**Unsupported `--include`, `--status`, `--kind`, or `--types` value.** A value outside a read's supported set is rejected before any request: stderr names the unsupported value and the supported set, and the command exits `2`. The tree read's `--include` set is `accountabilities, domains, members`; the role and subroles reads use the larger role include set; `domain --include` accepts only `policies`; `projects --status` accepts the seven project statuses; `subrole-actors --kind` accepts `agent`/`human`; `search --types` accepts the eight resource types.

**Filter or flag used on the wrong read.** A list filter passed with a single-resource id (`glassfrog roles role_0123 --tag marketing`), a list flag on a single read (`--query` on `domain`, `policy`, or `project`), `--depth` on `subroles`, or `--first-page`/`--per-page` on `tree` or a single read is a usage error: stderr names the misuse, no request is sent, and the command exits `2`.

**Unquoted multi-word search.** `glassfrog search strategy review` is read as two positionals and rejected with a usage error (exit `2`). Quote the whole query, exclusions included: `glassfrog search "strategy review -archived"`.

**Incomplete list.** If a list, roll-up, or search walk cannot retrieve every page, the results gathered so far are printed and stderr carries an explicit incomplete note naming the cause; the command exits non-zero. With `--first-page`, stderr instead notes that more results exist and the command exits `0` — re-run without `--first-page` to fetch all. Under `json`/`yaml`, a command-execution failure is written as the unified error envelope on **stdout** (so an agent parses success and failure the same way); under `full`/`compact` the diagnostic goes to stderr. The one exception is a mid-walk failure that has already emitted a partial `{data:[…]}` document — there the partial document stays on stdout and the incompleteness note rides stderr in every format, with the non-zero exit code as the authoritative signal.
